claims.claim: Reviewers describe finding full matches as difficult outside of peak hours, leaving certain game modes with vacant lobbies.

citations.review_text:
How is this game still this good?

I genuinely don't understand how a game this old can still feel this alive.

The gunplay is fun, the heroes are insanely satisfying to play, the sound design is perfect, and the atmosphere is just pure Star Wars. You can spend one match fighting as a normal trooper and the next one running around as Vader, Luke, Maul or Anakin — and somehow it never gets boring.

And then there's the 40-player battles...

When the lobby is full, explosions are everywhere, starfighters are flying overhead, heroes are fighting in the middle of the battlefield and everyone is pushing toward the objective...

That's Star Wars.

My only real complaint is the player count. Finding full matches can sometimes be difficult, especially outside peak hours. It's honestly frustrating knowing how much potential this game still has.

EA really should bring this game back with proper support, new content, or even just a better server browser.

This game isn't dead.
It just needs players.

If you're a Star Wars fan and you've never played this, you're seriously missing out.

Man...I still love this game. I played a ton of hours on playstation before I bought it on pc. Legit one of my favorite multiplayer Star Ears game.

I would say you have to look out when playing other multiplayer modes besides co-op as you may enter hacked lobbies or encounter cheating players. Many of the more niche game modes have vacant lobbies but the core modes still have reasonably filled lobbies.

Highly recommend it to any SW fan.

Great game, wouldnt believe its almost 10y old
but matchmaking is hell

One of the best team shooters of the modern era; HOWEVER I cannot recommend because EA ended support leaving the game in a completely broken state. Every game has one of three issues: 1. everyone in the match gets their camera locked to a random direction every few minutes which forces everyone to respawn and decides matches by effectively wiping all heroes on the field. 2. No battle points or XP is awarded so everyone can only choose from the 4 base classes (these are the best matches unfortunately). 3. lack of players in general, some modes will have you stuck waiting for hours and require high numbers of players to begin the match. The game is slowly dying and will eventually reach the point where modes like galactic assault and starfighter assault can no longer be played as they cannot be played with bots. EA needs to release a patch fixing all the bugs, it's ridiculous for a game to degrade so rapidly like this when it isn't being actively developed

So far so good, i can't really recommend a dead game. Maybe it's the modders that keep this game alive and that's why the steam charts have a ,,Currently Online Players 2'387'', otherwise, meeeh i'm outta here.

I am just baffled at how good this game is, for how dead it's online population is. And for the latter, confused as all hell as to why this game is still $40. 
If you want to play alone a majority of the time doing 1p missions, story, etc, it's great.
If you want to play multiplayer, you have to hit peak player times in order to play with maybe 7-12 other people. Otherwise your queues just go on forever and you spend more time per hour waiting around than actually playing. 

This is really disappointing. It's a great game, but it isn't worth $40 with it's current player population.

STAR WARS Battlefront II (2017) is a massive multiplayer shooter that drops players directly into the cinematic battles across all three major Star Wars eras.

Pros
* Spectacular visual and audio design that perfectly captures the authentic cinematic atmosphere of the Star Wars universe.
* Includes a massive roster of playable iconic heroes and villains, from Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader to Rey and Kylo Ren.
* Complete removal of the controversial launch microtransactions, meaning all gameplay elements, guns, and heroes are unlocked entirely through natural progression.
* Offers diverse gameplay modes, ranging from 40-player Galactic Assault to intense space dogfights in Starfighter Assault and large-scale tactical battles in Capital Supremacy.
* Features a highly polished, canonical single-player story campaign that bridges the narrative gap between Return of the Jedi and The Force Awakens.
* Offline Instant Action and co-op bot modes provide excellent replay-ability for casual players who want to practice without entering competitive lobbies.
* Playable characters include Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, Leia Organa, Chewbacca, Lando Calrissian, Rey, Yoda, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, Finn, BB-8, Boba Fett, Darth Vader, Emperor Palpatine, Bossk, Kylo Ren, Darth Maul, Captain Phasma, General Grievous, Count Dooku, BB-9E, and Iden Versio.

Cons
* Valve and EA anti-cheat protection is minimal, leading to a persistent and highly frustrating issue with hackers and invincibility exploits in public PC lobbies.
* The matchmaking system can be incredibly unbalanced, often pitting brand-new players against veterans who have maxed-out Star Card upgrades.
* Official developer support and content updates ended completely in 2020, meaning no new maps, heroes, or balance patches are being developed.
* Star Card progression system creates a distinct gameplay advantage for high-level players, granting them faster ability cooldowns and health buffs.

citations.review_text: Crawling with cheaters. Made by EA. What do you expect?

This game is amazing as a concept, and though its launch was a little rough, it managed to push past its growing pains and became the best multiplayer hero shooter set in the SW universe by far. DICE managed to make the game look stellar while running on modest hardware, and it made getting heros and specialists less of an RNG coin toss and more based on getting kills or doing objectives.
Unfortunately, the game requires a decent amount of grind in order to get good abilities for your characters, as practically everyone left in this game is a legacy player with their Star Cards maxed out and all their weapons leveled to the max. Despite this, this game is basically the only one out there that will satisfy your itch for a SW hero shooter.

However, to address the big elephant in the room, this game was abandoned by EA in order to focus on the Battlefield franchise, meaning this game receives no dev support. If you load into a game and there is a hacker running around, you have to leave and rejoin another match and hope they arent with you. There is no telling when the servers for this game will shutdown, and since this game is no longer supported by the devs, getting a match on a weekday or non-peak hours can take a VERY long time. 

With that in mind, I do not recommend this game if you want continued support or updates. However, if you are willing to take the risk, this game is the pretty much the best (and only) star wars multiplayer shooter game out there.

This game is amazing as a concept, and though its launch was a little rough, it managed to push past its growing pains and became the best multiplayer hero shooter set in the SW universe by far. DICE managed to make the game look stellar while running on modest hardware, and it made getting heros and specialists less of an RNG coin toss and more based on getting kills or doing objectives.
Unfortunately, the game requires a decent amount of grind in order to get good abilities for your characters, as practically everyone left in this game is a legacy player with their Star Cards maxed out and all their weapons leveled to the max. Despite this, this game is basically the only one out there that will satisfy your itch for a SW hero shooter.

However, to address the big elephant in the room, this game was abandoned by EA in order to focus on the Battlefield franchise, meaning this game receives no dev support. If you load into a game and there is a hacker running around, you have to leave and rejoin another match and hope they arent with you. There is no telling when the servers for this game will shutdown, and since this game is no longer supported by the devs, getting a match on a weekday or non-peak hours can take a VERY long time. 

With that in mind, I do not recommend this game if you want continued support or updates. However, if you are willing to take the risk, this game is the pretty much the best (and only) star wars multiplayer shooter game out there.

This is one of my favorite games of all time. I really love Star Wars. After the game stopped getting updates, it declined and the player count started going down. It’s really sad because the game is really good. The Heroes mode is fun, especially fighting other Force users, Darth Vader mogs. Conquest is also a fun mode. There are many more game modes. It has so much content I could go on and on about it, especially playing through the Age of the Republic to the Age of the Resistance. I hope they make Battlefront 3 in the future. It’s the most peak first-person shooter game and third person shooter, I suppose.

10/10
